text: Are there plans to expand outreach, such as partnering with community groups to better engage parents from diverse backgrounds?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Will there be structured policies to encourage help-seeking while addressing students' concerns about stigma or future repercussions?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: As we continue to strengthen mental health support for youths, what further steps will MOE take to empower parents to safeguard their children's well-being?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chair, MOE thanks Members for their suggestions, comments and support.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our education system has achieved much, but much is at stake.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Much more needs to be done for us to stay relevant, stay ahead and stay together.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have built a system that has uplifted our people amidst the challenges and opportunities through the years, and we have fostered a sense of cohesion and unity amongst Singaporeans, despite our diverse heritage and backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can easily be bypassed if we become irrelevant, overtaken if we become complacent and disrupted if we fail to understand the pivotal forces shaping our world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our goals remain unchanged: for Singapore to defy the odds of history to survive and thrive; for our people to be the best versions of themselves; and for us to distinguish ourselves by our ideals of excellence, our unity and our unyielding spirit to overcome challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But our approach, policies and mindsets must continue to evolve with the times.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As the global order fragments and geopolitical tensions worsen, we need to hone our ability to bridge divides, connect diverse perspectives and forge partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As economies become increasingly volatile and protectionist, we need to secure our relevance by adapting to new contexts, creating new value propositions and finding answers to tomorrow's questions ahead of time.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As societies fracture amidst rising inequality, heightened insecurities and divisive contestation in the information space, we need to strengthen our identity amidst these divisive forces to stay resilient and united, recognising that the competition is not amongst ourselves, but between Team Singapore and the rest of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As technology progresses and challenges convention, we need to master the new while integrating the best of the old to create breakthroughs in how we learn, teach and earn our keep.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Ms Denise Phua asked how we will provide a future-ready education for all.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I will focus on two structural shifts we have embarked on to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need to shift away from the narrow definitions of success, which may make us proficient in select domains but brittle as a system.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We must also avoid "teaching to the average", which does not bring out the best in anyone.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Instead, we must do better, by empowering Singaporeans to build on their different strengths, pursue excellence in their respective fields and contribute to society in their own ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, we have continually evolved our education system to meet the diverse and growing needs of all Singaporeans and to ensure that every child in our country has the opportunity to grow, blossom and realise their full potential, regardless of their starting point in life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will focus on two areas MOE will do more in.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we will strengthen support for students with SEN.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we will expand and enhance our post-secondary pathways to ensure that students can find different avenues to succeed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han, Mr Darryl David, Ms Denise Phua and Mr Patrick Tay have asked about our support for students with SEN in their education journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chair, the needs of our students with SEN are varied and multifaceted and require support from the whole of community, including MOE, Government agencies and SSAs, at different stages of their journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong shared the Government's plans to support persons with disabilities in their work and daily lives as part of this year's Budget.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I will focus on our efforts during the schooling years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: My MSF colleagues will touch on the support provided in the workplace and the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE's priority is to provide good education for students with SEN, whether they attend a mainstream or SPED schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: That is, 80% of our SEN students attend mainstream schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We start by ensuring that these children have a strong start in their education journey, as we do for their peers in our mainstream schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Well before their primary school years, MOE collaborates with hospitals to guide parents and caregivers on choosing suitable school settings and support to meet their child's needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During the preschool years, children with developmental needs can also participate in early intervention programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These programmes are specifically designed to provide additional support for children in areas, such as speech and language, social skills and motor skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I encourage parents to tap on these avenues and work with relevant healthcare and early childhood professionals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Early engagement between parents and professionals often leads to better outcomes, allowing us to provide the right support at the earliest opportunity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: By addressing these needs early, we lay a strong foundation for the future learning journey of these students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have put in additional resources for children with less-severe SEN and who can access the national curriculum to make a smoother transition into mainstream schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One example is the TRANsition Support for Integration (TRANSIT), which we launched in 2021 to support schools in preparing children who may need additional support as they enter Primary 1.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: By 2026, we will extend TRANSIT to all primary schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In mainstream schools, our teachers undergo training to support our diverse learners in the classroom before they enter the teaching service.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There are also around eight teachers with additional training in special needs in every primary and secondary schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, all primary and secondary schools have SEN officers who work closely with teachers, school counsellors and parents to support the students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I want to assure Members that we are continually strengthening our support for our SEN officers by providing access to professional development opportunities to enhance their skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For students enrolled in SPED schools, we agree with Mr Patrick Tay on the importance of working closely with partner agencies, SSAs and families to support their diverse needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our priority is ensuring that students, teachers and leaders across all SPED schools have access to the same kind of developmental opportunities and support, as do their colleagues in our mainstream schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We can only achieve this by moving together, not as 25 separate SPED schools but as one SPED sector, so that we can maximise the potential of the SPED ecosystem and better support our SPED students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is why we have strengthened our collaborations with the SPED sector over the years to enhance the accessibility and quality of education in our SPED schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we will continue to raise the quality of curriculum in our SPED schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the past, there was no common curriculum among our SPED schools as each SSA leading their school developed their own curriculum.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This resulted in diverse teaching and learning practices as well as schooling experiences for their students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Between 2020 and 2024, we worked closely with our SPED schools to co-develop and implement seven SPED Teaching and Learning Syllabuses (TLS), giving more detailed guidance to the overarching SPED curriculum framework articulated in 2012.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These syllabuses were progressively introduced across diverse domains – from visual arts to social-emotional learning as well as communication and language.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With the completion of TLS in 2024, we now have a national SPED curriculum across all SPED schools to pave the next lap of excellence in teaching and learning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Having visited several SPED schools, I am personally encouraged by how our SPED practitioners, both educators and allied professionals, have leveraged the curriculum to deliver engaging lessons that meet the wide-ranging students' needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we will partner with schools to better integrate digital tools in our SPED schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, we have a range of technologies and applications to reduce the workload of teachers in our mainstream schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, for example, we have applications that facilitate communication between teachers and parents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some of us who are parents, who are in schools today, we know that teachers will be familiar with using Parents Gateway to liaise with parents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our SPED schools, on the other hand, have different systems and processes to manage their administrative work because they are different organisations with different needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We need to study this carefully though, to account for the diverse needs of our SPED students, parents as well as our SPED teachers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, a parent of a child with SEN will have a significantly different admissions process and experience from a parent with a child in a mainstream school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While the process of applying to a mainstream school can be largely automated, SPED schools will need additional information from parents and professionals to better understand the child's needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will explore this collaboration, introduce these digital solutions and will share the outcomes when they are ready.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, we will work closely with our partners in the community to strengthen the collective expertise and professional creed among our SPED educators.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have worked with SSAs to progressively set up SPED Communities of Practice (COPs) as a platform for practitioners in schools, educators and SSAs to collaborate professionally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, MOE's support for students with SEN does not stop at schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also ensure that they transition well into higher education and the workplace.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: An increasing number of students with SEN progress from our mainstream and SPED schools into our post-secondary education institutions, including our ITEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, ITE has a strong ecosystem in place to help students with SEN maximise their potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These include dedicated SEN Support Officers and Education and Career Coaches as well as partners like SG Enable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To strengthen support for students with SEN to transit from classrooms to the workplace, ITE and SG Enable started a programme last year to provide them with further internship and employment support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was what Mr Darryl David had asked earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Under this programme, students with SEN undergo training in areas, such as personal grooming, resume writing and interview preparation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These students are then placed in suitable internship roles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Members would be pleased to know that ITE and SGE work very closely with participating students and employers to ensure that these internships are calibrated to meet the students' learning needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One student, for example, in this programme, is Joseph, a Year 2 student with autism spectrum disorder and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder in ITE's Higher Nitec in Retail and Online Business course.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ITE helped Joseph secure an internship at the Uniqlo outlet at Waterway Point.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Joseph initially had found it difficult to adjust to the work environment with high footfall and busy operations throughout the day.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To support Joseph, a job coach from TOUCH Community Services visited him weekly at the store to train him on work skills, including communication, problem solving and interpersonal skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The coaches was assigned personally to attend to students, like Joseph, during the internship experience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: He was also given opportunities by Uniqlo to learn and apply these skills around the store.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Two months into the internship, Joseph had grown significantly and was awarded Best Customer Service Award by the store, just within two months of his internship.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are very pleased with that and we hope more students like Joseph will benefit from internship opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, ITE and SGE are working closely to scale-up the programme to benefit more students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Denise Phua asked about supporting continuing education for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, their learning needs are diverse and complex, as we all know.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition to specialised training opportunities curated by SGE, we have been working with training providers to make mainstream training programmes more accessible to persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More importantly, the lifelong learning ecosystem for these individuals must be well-integrated with inclusive employment models and opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is why we take a whole-of-society approach, with MSF and SGE taking the lead to support their lifelong learning journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Joseph's journey illustrates how an ecosystem of educators, employers, dedicated agencies and job coaches can come together to support learning, internship and employment opportunities for SEN individuals.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hope that there will be more of such stories as we work together to build an inclusive society.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, beyond supporting those in need, we will also provide multiple pathways to meet the diverse aspirations of our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For our students at their post-secondary level, we want to equip them with work-ready skills to thrive in the future economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For ITE students, we have made good progress in curriculum redesign.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This curricular redesign streamlined the two-year Nitec plus the two-year Higher Nitec structure, providing a more integrated pathway to equip our ITE students with deeper skills and a robust foundation for future skills upgrading.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The first cohort graduates this July and has enjoyed the rigorous curriculum and extended industry attachments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope they will enter the workforce empowered with a renewed sense of confidence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More students can look forward to these experiences, as ITE transitions all remaining courses to the enhanced structure next year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our support for ITE students also continues after they graduate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I congratulate all of our 12,000 ITE graduates who have benefited from the IPA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This means that the IPA will be extended to more courses beyond those offered by ITE and the polytechnics.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These WSQ diplomas are aligned to the Skills Framework and allow individuals to acquire skills and credentials to access good jobs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With this expansion, more than 30 diploma programmes will be eligible for the IPA, on top of the 300 eligible programmes that we already have today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, for polytechnic students, we piloted new ways of learning, such as flexible curriculum workloads for students and short-term work attachments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over 1,000 students have participated in these pilots, with nine in 10 reporting that these programmes have helped them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Learning from the pilots, all our polytechnics will allow all students to customise their curriculum load.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also work with institutions to provide students with a range of industry exposure opportunities earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond these efforts, we will encourage our polytechnic students to explore their interests and develop skills along the way through CEPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Under the CEP, students can explore different specialisations within a sector through a common semester, before deciding on a diploma of their choice.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Wan Rizal would be happy to know that since its launch in 2017, the number of CEPs has increased over four times to 25 today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They collectively provide access to 75% of all diplomas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While students can still choose specialised diplomas directly, the number of students entering CEPs has also increased to 25% of each polytechnic cohort, up from 10% in 2017.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to work with our institutions to innovate and provide space for students to broaden their exposure and competencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: From AY2025, all schools in Republic Polytechnic (RP) will offer a broad-based diploma option for students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They will cater to students who desire to both engage in multidisciplinary learning within their cluster and gain specialised skills through a selected major.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, rather than specialising in a specific domain of engineering, such as aviation or robotics, students can choose to enter the Diploma in Engineering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While of the same duration as other diplomas, which is three years, this diploma provides broad-based training in essential skills related to the engineering sector like design, programming and data analysis, allowing students to major in Innovation and Design, Project Management and Sustainable Technology, depending on their interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: After graduating, students will have the flexibility to take on a wider range of jobs across different engineering domains.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this case, students will also have the option to pursue minors to broaden their knowledge or deepen their expertise in their respective disciplines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, we hope the RP experience will spur other polytechnics to also consider new opportunities for their respective students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to very quickly continue in Malay.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Chairman, after 60 years of Independence, we continue to invest in the education of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to work hard to support the diverse aspirations of students, strengthen support for students with different needs and enhance post-secondary education pathways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With Singapore's rapidly changing economic landscape, Singaporeans need to be constantly ready to upgrade themselves with new skills to remain relevant in the working world – by embodying lifelong learning in themselves and their lives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are deeply concerned and understand the challenges faced by families with children who have special needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Their journey is difficult, but they remain steadfast in facing the demands of raising their children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also recognise the importance of deepening students' interest in their mother tongue languages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will also expose them to a variety of literary texts and complex issues, to deepen their appreciation towards Malay culture and expand their worldview.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope more of our graduates can make skills upgrading a theme in their lifelong learning journey. : Mr Chairman, to conclude, MOE is committed to ensuring that all children, regardless of their background, have the opportunity to reach their fullest potential, with great care and attention, and in partnership with parents and teachers, and our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will ensure that the seeds we plant in our education system today grow into a thriving Singapore for generations to come.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, our nation's SkillsFuture story started in 2015.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our aim was to help Singaporeans develop to their fullest potential throughout life and also to build a fair and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In the same year, we introduced the SkillsFuture Credit Scheme, giving $500 to Singaporeans, to empower adults to continue to learn, upskill and reskill, whether in their early career, mid-career or silver years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Singaporeans use the Credit to improve their employment prospects or simply to pursue their interests and acquire skills to lead more fulfilling lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In 2020, we embarked on the Next Bound of SkillsFuture to strengthen enterprise ownership of upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is challenging but necessary to strengthen the link between individual upskilling, employment outcomes and business competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We stepped up efforts to support employers in building up workplace learning and capabilities in upskilling their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This marked a key shift to engage industry leaders as queen bees to uplift their sectors with skills advisory and training support for companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: ST Engineering Land Systems Ltd is the latest appointed SkillsFuture Queen Bee, supporting the precision engineering sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It will work with National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Company Training Committee, allowing companies in precision engineering to also benefit from NTUC's expertise and resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This deliberate shift in focus has seen results.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: More than 40% of the subsidies went to trainees who were sponsored by their companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Companies that sponsored workers for training also saw positive returns in productivity, as seen in a Ministry of Trade and Industry study in 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In line with these efforts, the Government has been stepping up expenditure on CET, from $0.5 billion in 2015, to more than $1 billion in 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: With the investments, we significantly enhanced our landscape of industry-relevant training programmes, catering to training needs for adults across different ages, professions and sectors, and we have helped more individuals and employers access such training through enhanced subsidies, especially for mid-careerists and SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: While the training participation rate of the resident labour force fell, we saw an increase in the number of employees sponsored by their companies for SSG-supported training programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In 2024, more than 550,000 individuals, and that is about one-fifth of our local workforce, took up training with subsidies from SSG, about a 7% increase compared to 2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har suggested that we target funding at programmes with stronger employment outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In fact, SSG has already moved in this direction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: From this year, the highest level of SSG's funding is given only to courses that deliver strong manpower outcomes, such as the SkillsFuture Work-Study Programmes which combine classroom learning with structured on-the-job training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Today, SkillsFuture has become one of the key pillars of our refreshed social compact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The success of the SkillsFuture movement must ultimately be measured by whether Singaporeans have the confidence and competence to seize emerging opportunities in life and also whether enterprises can find skilled workers among the local workforce to capture new business opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To this end, we must continue to strengthen the key partnerships between employers, individuals and training providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: They are the cornerstone of the SkillsFuture movement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: First, deepening the involvement of employers in skills development and training must remain a key priority.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers complement the Government in skills investment and create enabling conditions to support workers' upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: They help inform individuals' training decisions when they identify their skills needs and articulate them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers can also create greater confidence for workers when they recognise the skills and competencies attained.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will double down on our current suite of support measures in helping employers and enterprises, especially SMEs, take relevant skills action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We cannot achieve this alone and will require the partnerships of our sector intermediaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For example, we are piloting Jobs-Skills Integrators in the precision engineering, retail and wholesale trade sectors that have higher concentrations of SMEs and mature workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Job-Skills Integrators (JSITs) play a critical role in identifying jobs and skills needs in the sector, connecting employers with appropriate solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Skechers Singapore is a company that has benefited from this pilot.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Working with JSIT-Retail, led by the Singapore National Employers Federation, in partnership with the NTUC and WSG, Skechers implemented redesigned job roles and training, to streamline and automate its inventory tracking and goods retrieval system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Skechers successfully achieve a higher productivity operating model and upskilled its workers to take on higher-value roles such as data analysis and route planning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Encouraging employers to adopt skills-first HR practices will be a key next bound focus.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To support that, WSG and SSG have launched Career Health SG, which seeks to equip employers with tools and resources to support skills-first hiring and develop their workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: More details on the initiative will be progressively rolled out in this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Career Health SG also signals a key shift to bridge careers and skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Through the initiative, we hope to empower individuals to plan their careers and chart their careers and skills journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: More details on the Career Health SG will be covered in the MOM COS segment today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To support individuals taking ownership, we have expanded opportunities in upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked whether entry criteria to certain local universities could be eased to take in all students as long as they meet the absolute entry criteria.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I want to say that since the expansion of the Lifetime Cohort Participation Rate from 2023, we have seen more students admitted to our AUs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This means that more Singaporeans have the opportunity to take up significant training, not just at 18 years old but throughout their lives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our approach is not to perpetuate a paper chase.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Rather, our approach is to support purposeful, timely attainment of relevant knowledge and skills, with the qualification serving to reflect the mastery attained.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We remain committed to providing opportunities to realise the diverse strengths and aspirations of our students, while keeping in mind the needs of our economy and employers' confidence in the quality of our graduates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have significantly enhanced training support for mid-career Singaporeans aged 40 and above, who are at higher risk of skills obsolescence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To ensure that the Credit utilisation ultimately supports meaningful careers as pointed out by Ms Foo Mee Har and Ms Mariam Jaafar, we have curated over 7,000 courses with stronger employability outcomes, including market-recognised full qualifications and their stackable micro-credential constituents offered by the IHLs and SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme (SCTP) courses and so on.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG will work with sector agencies, industry and training providers to provide these courses and to refresh them regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is to ensure that the courses are of high quality and can support economic and manpower needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Song Wentao who is 56 this year is one beneficiary of the SkillsFuture (Mid-Career) top-up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: After 30 years in the defence and maritime industries, Mr Song's role was unfortunately made redundant during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: He saw the potential to make a meaningful career switch, choosing the healthcare sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: He took up a five-month SCTP in Therapy Support at the HMI Institute.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: After receiving 90% course fee subsidies, he fully offset the remaining out-of-pocket fees of $1,300 using the $4,000 SkillsFuture (Mid-Career).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Song graduated from the course in September last year and is now working as a Therapy Assistant at St Andrew's Community Hospital where he finds meaning in supporting elderly stroke patients in their rehabilitation journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: From next year, we will further extend the training allowance to selected part-time training, fixed at $300 per month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Eligible part-time programmes will include part-time SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme and part-time full qualifications and the stackable micro-credentials constituents offered by our IHLs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On Dr Wan Rizal's question on support for lower-wage workers' training, MOM will enhance the Workfare's Skills Support to provide a similar monthly training allowance to lower-wage workers aged 30 and above who pursue long form full-time or part-time training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These support measures I have mentioned also apply to freelancers that Ms See Jinli Jean asked about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Freelancers aged 40 and above could use the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit to offset their out-of-pocket training fees and also apply for the training allowance when pursuing training full-time or part-time training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Patrick Tay suggested consolidating the CET ecosystem to break down programme silos.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Today, we have taken a market-driven approach, allowing diverse training providers – IHLs, accredited CET Centres and private training providers – to provide training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This has helped to expand CET capacity and enabled the CET system to be responsive to diverse and evolving needs of different sectors and CET learners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are also continually improving our sign-posting of training opportunities for both individuals and employers, so that they may better navigate the ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Just as important, we must push for higher quality and professional standards within the Training and Adult Education sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These are currently being studied and we hope to share more soon.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Before I conclude, I would like to quote our former Deputy Prime Minister Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam, who first spoke on SkillsFuture in 2014.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: He said: "We must be a place where everyone has the opportunity to build on their strengths, developing the skills that enable them to maximise their potential, earn their own success and contribute to society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It's about respecting the innate dignity of every citizen – the sense of fulfilment that comes from playing their full role and being valued for their contributions to society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is the way we create a truly inclusive society." Mr Tharman's vision of SkillsFuture remains relevant today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Government will play an enabling and integrator role.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Together, we can help every Singaporean realise their potential and enable businesses to thrive, even in an age of disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank fellow Members for their passion towards students' development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Ms Denise Phua spoke about students' health habits and Mr Gerald Giam called for sporting opportunities for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Our students experience diverse sports in Physical Education (PE) lessons, exploring which sport best spurs their passion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This will drive them to pursue it and keep active throughout life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Most schools also work with SportSG to offer the Sports Education Programme to further increase quality sports programmes for our students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: CCAs remain key platforms where students discover their interests and talents and develop strong character.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To better cater to student interest, most primary schools do not conduct CCA selection trials.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: While schools seek to provide a good range of CCA options to cater to students' varied interests, a lack of critical mass may prevent them from providing more CCAs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For example, Suresh Amirthanathan Tharshika, a Secondary 2 student from Broadrick Secondary School, was talent-spotted by her PE teacher after a school race.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: However, her school did not offer Athletics CCA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This is why students like Tharshika welcome the Strategic Partnership CCA (SP-CCA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: SP-CCA widens the choice of CCA for students beyond what is offered by their secondary schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Under the guidance of coaches from the SP-CCA, she will be participating in her first National School Games Track and Field Championships this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Micah Choo is a student from Pasir Ris Secondary School.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: After two years in the SP-CCA Water Polo programme team, he grew in leadership skills and is now one of the CCA leaders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Micah met teammates like John Chia from Bukit View Secondary School and Zacharia Teng from Fairfield Methodist Secondary School.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Although from different schools, these boys forged strong friendships beyond the pool.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: When Micah struggled with Mathematics, John helped him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Micah did the same for John with Humanities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Finding the right coaches and instructors for CCA is just as critical.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: They play a significant role in students' development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Edward Chia raised a point on procurement for coaches.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The Government Electronic Business portal (GeBIZ), allows all instructors the opportunity to bid fairly for CCA services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOE has been working closely with the NICA to address some of the issues raised by the Member and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Miss Rachel Ong and Ms Denise Phua highlighted their concerns over students' mental health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Today, the impact of excessive and inappropriate social media use on children and adolescents' mental health is a widespread concern.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Schools play a key role equipping every child with competencies to grow to be the best version of themselves – be it in their relationships, educational pursuits, or in the digital world.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) curriculum has emphasis on Mental Health and Cyber Wellness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For example, students learn self-regulation techniques, interpersonal skills and problem-solving strategies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: They learn to maintain a healthy balance of online and offline activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: For younger students, we encourage tighter screen controls.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: There are also initiatives, such as the annual Safer Internet Day, to promote screen-free time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Schools appoint dedicated personnel to oversee cyber-related issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: And when the need arises, schools connect students with counselling or mental health professionals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Parents play a critical role in their child's well-being, complementing efforts in school.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: But not all parents may be aware of their children's difficulties.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: The Media Literacy Council and TOUCH Community Services polled parents in 2022 and found that 38% of parents with children aged between seven and 17 struggled to get their child to share about their online activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Hence, the Parenting for Wellness Initiative was developed by MOE, MSF and the Health Promotion Board (HPB) under the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy to empower parents to, firstly, build strong parent-child relationships; two, support their child's mental health and emotional resilience; and three, parent effectively in the digital age.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked for updates on Parenting for Wellness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To date, there are three different resources catering to parents with different needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: First, the Toolbox for Parents is a digital resource comprising bite-sized, just-in-time actionable strategies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Second, parents who prefer more personalised support may log onto the Parenting for Wellness website on Health Hub.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Third, the Conversation Card Deck helps parents and their children to have good conversations and deepen their mutual understanding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Copies are available via the schools' Parent Support Groups.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Parents appreciate Parenting for Wellness for its practicality, comprehensiveness and relevance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOE's Student Welfare Officers also found the Parenting for Wellness resources beneficial.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: They are keen to use it in their work with families to support needy students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Collaborations across the Government, community and industry partners are essential to support our children's mental wellness.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Students in mainstream and SPED schools learn to appreciate the importance of an active and healthy lifestyle through PE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This is a new national health promotion strategy to enhance preventive care and inculcate healthier lifestyles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: This includes cultivating good nutrition, exercise, device use and sleep habits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: To Ms Denise Phua, these efforts lay the foundational habits for students to sustain a healthy, active lifestyle after they graduate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Ong Hua Han raised the issue of financial literacy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: MOE has incorporated financial literacy into the school curriculum.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
text: Mr Chairman, MOE will continue to work collectively with our partners to provide all our students the opportunities to develop their strengths and talents, catered to their needs, regardless of their start points in life.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: I have met people like Ms Pooja from EveryChild.SG, who has feedback on one key systemic change to have smaller class sizes of 25 or fewer for children in primary school.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Has MOE done a study and assess what is the ideal best class size to achieve maximum education outcomes?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: The second clarification for Minister of State Gan is in relation to the skills-based hiring.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: How does MOE as well as SkillsFuture Singapore intend to nudge more employers, especially to implement skills-based hiring and employment practices?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: You need to get them on board to recognise that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is often a proposed solution, but I thought it is important for us to bear in mind what problems we are trying to solve first.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And what class size should we aim for – 30, 20, 10?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Is our problem statement the need to improve teacher-student interaction or is our problem statement to reduce teachers' workload, or is it because we believe that smaller is better, regardless of the subject being taught or the teachers' quality?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We all want to reduce the workload for our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But with a finite teaching force and a certain number of students, do we mean to ask our teachers to teach smaller classes but more classes?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Or do we mean that we should employ more teachers, perhaps doubling our teaching force to halve all class sizes?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Is that the best way to use our teaching resources, even if we assume we can double our recruitment from broadly what is now about 2% of every cohort to 4% of every cohort?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Or do we mean for our teachers to teach less?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have benchmarked our curriculum with other developed countries.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are already teaching just similar amounts, or sometimes less, compared to others.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we often hear calls for MOE to include more in our curriculum, including from many Members today in your speeches, to have more life skills, future skills, soft skills, to prepare our students better for life.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Most form classes have two form teachers to guide the socio-emotional development of our children, compared to one in the past when we were in school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Students with higher needs have smaller teaching class size.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Classes that benefit from students' interaction have bigger class sizes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For classes that we can use technology to scale, we have even "bigger class sizes" in the hundreds and yet achieve mass customisation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, Chair, indeed, we want to refocus our teachers' energies to not over protect students or over support training.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Instead, we want our students to exercise agency in organising activities and take more responsibilities for their learning.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And in this way, they learn more for life.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, we share the goals for more personalised teaching, more personal attention for every student and more focused work for our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think we can all agree on that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, I am one for aspiring to organise our teaching resources to achieve the effective class size of one, where we need but not regardless of need.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: An effective class size of one, where we need, but not regardless of need.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us focus the discussion on how we can achieve this through the following ways: (a) the way we focus our teachers' effort in doing what is necessary for our students and not overdoing things; (b) the way we use technology to complement our teachers' capabilities to scale up quality resources at affordable cost; (c) the way we equip our teachers to do their best for our students; (d) the way we teach our students to exercise agency and responsibility in their learning journeys; and (e) the way we partner our teachers to set the right expectations for ourselves and our teachers.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked how he can nudge more employers to take on skills-based hiring and employment practices.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I think we need to understand the "why" and the "how" for the employers.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We know that Singapore has a very tight labour market.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I need a diploma in that", which are very broad and maybe not very sharp in defining the skills that they really need.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: By taking on skills-based hiring, employers can better find employees that meet their business needs and make the business more competitive.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, the "why" is something that we are working on.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The Career Health SG that I mentioned earlier on, something that WSG and SSG are working on to get more employers on board, is an exciting development.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is not going to be an easy feat.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Indeed, a lot of effort needs to be put in to help employers see the benefits of this programme.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The other thing that I want to bring up would be leveraging Queen Bees, for example, and also the skills development partners.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: And individuals who go for such training are being recognised by employers.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I think this type of collaboration is helpful to get employers to see the benefits of skills-based hiring.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: HR is another group that we need to develop for them to be able to support the employers and co-workers in understanding the benefits and operationalising skills-based hiring.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, there are lots of work that we need to do in addition to the very long list of things I mentioned in my speech earlier on on how we can support employers to take on skills-based hiring.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Denise Phua, make it short, so that I can squeeze one or two more in, if possible.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I accept that Singapore's starting point and our culture are different.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: What is so special about us that we cannot do this so that we can free up more time for the development of the 21st century skills that MOE proposes?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, we thank Ms Denise Phua and various Members for your well-intentioned suggestions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, we constantly challenge ourselves to relook our own assumptions and come up with and consider new ideas, whether they are from our fraternity of educators, Members of this House, members of the public or experiences of other countries.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But our approach must first correctly define the problem before we go into solutioning.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The through-train proposal from primary to secondary school idea, as Ms Denise Phua said, is not new.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Other countries have variations of it, with varying outcomes depending on their goals.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And one can even make the argument that the affiliated schools in Singapore are a variant of this idea.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The question is, what goals do we want to achieve in making this change?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Is it to remove high-stakes examinations for young children?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Is it to free up space and time for students to pursue other dimensions of growth as Ms Denise Phua mentioned?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Is it inclusiveness, so that our students experience the richness of the Singaporean community?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Is it to promote more social mixing in our schools?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Or is it all the above and more?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Then, we should ask ourselves: will a through-train achieve all this and what are the more fundamental issues that we have to grapple with?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Are we stressed because we cannot meet the standards we set for ourselves and our children, or are we stressed because we want to keep up with others in a rat race?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Would we end up shifting the competition for our preferred secondary school earlier to a preferred primary school through, say, a Primary 1 registration contest or even a preschool leaving examination?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if we continue to see examinations as a competition for preferred schools instead of right-siting our students for the next segment of their learning journey, then will removing PSLE alone solve the problem or will it concentrate the stakes at a even higher level, at the "O" level and "A" level stages?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if we do not post students to schools appropriate for their learning needs, how will we make better use of our finite resources to achieve the best holistic outcomes for different students?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if we remove one major examination but our mindsets do not change, will we gain more time and space for the diverse skill sets that we wish for our children, as I have shared in my story earlier during my speech?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the other hand, if we can truly change our mindsets to respect and pursue diverse strengths, then do we still need to focus narrowly on having or removing a single examination?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, today, we have already assured all of our children that regardless of the outcome in any particular examination, the pathways are porous enough for you to pivot into areas that you find your passion in subsequently in life.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If our society recognises and reward diverse skill sets, will we still pursue a narrow definition of success indicated by a PSLE or "O" level score?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As previously mentioned, the operational issues that we need to step through are not trivial.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Who gets to go into a through-train programme?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Who gets to decide whether a person can stay in a through-train programme?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Who gets to go in, who gets to go out?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, there are things that we need to step through and I thank Members for their support for the Ministry's work.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: No system is perfect in meeting everyone's desires and needs, but we try our best to provide every child with education options that meets his or her needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, I would like to share a slogan that is close to my heart, and this is called, "For every child, a good school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At every age, a good learner." "For every child, a good school", means that we do not need to go and chase after what other people desire as a popular school, but instead we put our children at the centre of all that we do and consider our children's needs and what is most appropriate for his or her learning needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That is why to me, "For every child, a good school." "At every age, a good learner", to go beyond just the first 15 years.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why we have embarked on multiple pathways of success.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why we continue to have social mixing to bring together children from different backgrounds in the same class, so that they learn to work with people from different backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is also why we have a more open Primary 1 registration process, where we balance the building of a school culture and tradition with the egalitarian ethos and culture of being non-exclusive that we so cherish as Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why we are adopting edtech to customise teaching and learning, so that we can transcend "teaching to the average" and achieve the effective class size of one, overcoming the conventional public education trilemma of achieving quality, scale and affordability at the same time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I think we can do that because today, with the science of learning, the technology and the data that we have, we have the best chance in the history of the education profession to break this trilemma.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I do not believe that we cannot change our mindsets.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Read my speech at the MOE x NIE x IPS seminar.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We can do it and we need these two to move in tandem, changing structures and processes with the changing of cultures and mindsets —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Chan, you may want to round up your closing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I was going to give you some time but we have run out of time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, can I invite Mr Patrick Tay, if you would like to withdraw the amendment.
